description: A delay and reverb built out of distances: an emitter and two listeners are placed inside a rectangular box, and the delay times come from how far the sound travels between them and off the four walls

params.text: Scales all of the calculated delay times together, from a few milliseconds at the far left to about twelve seconds at the far right; it is a multiplier on the distances, not a delay time
Sets how wide the box is, and with it how far apart the two side walls are
Sets how tall the box is, and with it how far apart the top and bottom walls are
Sets how much of the second reflection off the walls is fed back into the box, none at the far left
Scatters the feedback reflections in time by up to ten milliseconds of fixed random spread, none at the far left
Sets the corner of the lowpass filter in the feedback path, about 39Hz at the far left to 20kHz at the far right
Sets the corner of the highpass filter in the feedback path, about 39Hz at the far left to 20kHz at the far right
Pulls the direct sound forward so it arrives at the nearer listener immediately, and takes the same amount off the other; at the far left both direct paths keep their true delay

inputs.text: The audio going into the box
The return for that feedback path; with nothing patched the send is connected straight back to it inside the module
Shifts the delay scaling; a positive voltage shortens the delays rather than lengthening them
Shifts the box width, 10V covering the whole of that knob's travel
Shifts the box height, 10V covering the whole of that knob's travel
Shifts the feedback, 10V covering the whole of that knob's travel
Shifts the diffusion, one millisecond per volt

outputs.text: The sound reaching the first listener, both the reflections off the walls and the direct path
The sound reaching the second listener, both the reflections off the walls and the direct path
The feedback path tapped before it goes round again, for sending through other modules

notes: The emitter and the two listeners are dragged around the screen at the top of the panel: a yellow circle for the input, an orange square for the first output and a purple square for the second
Those three points are one display rather than separate controls, so no click on them reaches this help
This module is mono: it reads one channel from every jack and sends one channel out of each
